# Format-Preserving Invalid Identifiers

A replacement identifier has two jobs that pull against each other. It must **look like** the thing it
replaces, or every parser, regex, column width and human reader downstream breaks. It must **not be**
a valid instance of that thing, or you have minted an identifier that could collide with a real
person's.

The resolution used in [[labour-fraud-analysis]]: keep the shape, break the checksum.

| Identifier class | Shape kept | Validity broken by |
|---|---|---|
| Travel document | letter prefix + fixed-length digit body | no issuing-authority range, no check digit |
| National identity number | correct digit count | no checksum, and no date of birth encoded in the leading digits |
| Tax number | correct digit count | no checksum |
| Permit reference | serial / year / authority-suffix structure | fictional authority; serials offset by a constant |

The national identity number is the instructive case. Real numbers of that family encode a date of
birth in their leading digits and end in a check digit. The synthetic version has the right length and
nothing else — so it sorts, joins, displays and matches a length regex, while carrying no birth date
and failing any checksum routine. It is a *shape*, not an *identity*.

## Why the permit offset matters

Permit serials in a bulk filing are consecutive in the source, and that contiguity is a load-bearing
part of the [[convergent-evidence]] argument. A random remapping would destroy it. Adding a constant
offset to the whole batch preserves the *differences* between serials — the property the analysis
reads — while changing every value. Structure survives, identity does not:
[[structure-preserving-anonymisation]].

## Assert the invalidity, do not assume it

The property is only worth claiming if something checks it. Three tests in the suite do:

- national identifiers must not match a valid-checksum pattern (shape only — see the limitation
  below),
- no phone number may match the source-region shape,
- the currency in the dataset must be a fictional one.

These run on every push through [[github-actions]], unlike the parts of the [[disclosure-gate]] that
need the private source. Note the limitation plainly: the identity-number test checks a *shape*, not
that the value fails a real checksum algorithm — a value could in principle pass a real validator and
still pass this test. Recorded as a limit of the check, not a known failure.

## Transferable rule

When you must publish surrogate identifiers, decide up front which of the identifier's properties are
**syntactic** (length, alphabet, separators, sort order, adjacency) and which are **semantic**
(checksum, embedded date, issuing range, registry lookup). Preserve the first set; deliberately break
the second; then write a test for each break.
